repairs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE camera-corrected supplementary design view of the SAME spacecraft console.
Input image 1 is the authoritative four-view identity sheet (front/back/left/right). Input image 2 is the failed camera-angle candidate to correct. Change ONLY the observation direction to the requested exact orthographic plan view; preserve the existing device design, two instrument stations, exactly two integrated joystick grips, central service spine, two slim support columns and two shallow rectangular bolted feet. No new parts, no room, no people, no labels, no arrows, no text or watermark.
Pure white background, neutral even studio illumination, whole intact object centered with generous margins. Not exploded, not cutaway. The object is 2.30m wide and 0.90m deep in plan (about 2.56:1 width to depth), not a tall frontal silhouette. No perspective convergence. Surfaces parallel to the camera ray are edge-on, not shown as large faces.

Requested view: EXACT VERTICAL TOP PLAN, camera DIRECTLY ABOVE, looking straight DOWN along the support-column axes, zero yaw/tilt. Width horizontal, operator lip at BOTTOM, rear at TOP.
The failure in image 2 is that it exposes a large vertical rear vent wall and full-height upright screen faces. Those vertical wall faces MUST disappear or collapse to thin edge lines in a real top projection. The rear cabinet top cap is a shallow strip, not a second standing back wall. The sloping instrument faces are naturally foreshortened into their plan footprint. Upright joystick height is also foreshortened: see the tops and bellows rather than full upright side silhouettes. The desktop opaque housing normally hides the support columns/feet; do not move them outward to reveal them.
Produce a strictly flat overhead product photograph/parallel-projection plan. No oblique, front, rear, low-angle or elevated three-quarter rendition.
